prose: DeepSeek has released V4.1 Flash 1017, the October 17 snapshot of its V4.1 Flash model, served under the deepseek-flash API name. It is the first model built on the company's Causal Encoder-Decoder (CED) architecture: a sparse mixture-of-experts with a 552B-parameter backbone that activates only 8B parameters on input and 16B on output, keeping per-token compute low relative to total size.

Image understanding is native this time, with visual and text embeddings trained jointly from the start of pre-training rather than bolted on afterward. DeepSeek targets coding, terminal and computer-use agents plus long-horizon tasks, and says compressed KV caching cuts cache memory to roughly a quarter of the previous Flash generation, a direct cost lever on agentic workloads. The company positions Flash as the cost-efficient V4.1 tier while claiming it beats V4 Pro on performance, speed and task completion time.
highlights: First model on DeepSeek's Causal Encoder-Decoder (CED) architecture
552B backbone, activates 8B on input and 16B on output
Native image understanding trained jointly from pre-training start
Aimed at coding, terminal and computer-use agents and long-horizon tasks
Compressed KV cache uses about a quarter of prior Flash memory
Claimed to exceed V4 Pro on performance, speed and task completion
